analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 52132-53549). The file is a public golden-vector fixture of synthetic prompts ("Public synthetic cache-parity input"), template inputs, prompt_contract_id values, token_ids and block-boundary chain hashes. The change per file_changes and the patch excerpt is regeneration of fixture data. For example, an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} member was added to a template_input, prompt_token_count changed (803 to 767), and chain hashes and token IDs were updated. No executable code, auth, attestation, key handling, App Attest (TB-011, A-016) or coordinator-provider wire logic is touched. The fixture contains no secrets; all content is synthetic and public. Security relevance is indirect: these vectors pin the prompt-contract and prefix-cache block-hash behavior used by the encrypted prefix cache (T-041 cache-sharing and timing oracle). A change in the template (the enable_thinking context) and in the chain hashes could alter cache keying/partitioning. The diff is truncated and only base-side text was supplied, so the head-side values, the new prompt_contract_id, and the Swift/Go code that consumes and verifies these vectors (e.g. whether cache keys still bind scope_id and the contract id) were not visible. I cannot confirm that the generator and consumer remain consistent, so no finding is raised. The next pass should check that the prompt_contract_id is properly versioned, that scope_id remains bound into the chain hashes, and that the producing code changes (not in this batch) do not weaken cross-tenant cache isolation.
